events.title: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole keynote
events.why_it_matters: First Jackson Hole address by Chair Kevin Warsh (in office since May) with July PCE at 3.7% YoY, funds at 3.50–3.75%, and ~30–40% odds of a September hike.
events.what_to_watch: Whether he diagnoses inflation as persistent demand vs energy/tariff shock, and any shift vs his no-detailed-guidance stance; 10:00 a.m. ET livestream.

events.title: Jackson Hole symposium (financial innovation theme)
events.why_it_matters: Kansas City Fed symposium is the global central-bank huddle; regional presidents already used the sidelines to warn inflation is not falling fast enough.
events.what_to_watch: Hawkish dissenters vs Warsh framework remarks; any comments on payments, Treasury market functioning, or AI productivity as disinflation.

events.title: July PCE: 3.7% YoY, core 3.3%
events.why_it_matters: Fed's preferred inflation gauge was unchanged at 3.7% YoY (core 3.3%), hotter than ~3.6% consensus, lifting September hike odds into the mid-30s.
events.what_to_watch: How Warsh treats this print today; next CPI (Sep 11) and NFP (Sep 4) will decide if the Sep 16 FOMC hikes or holds.

events.title: Nvidia Q2 FY27 beat and $108B Q3 guide
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY), data center $89.0B, Q3 guide $108B ±2% with no China compute assumed — the AI-capex bellwether still accelerating.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through into Broadcom (Sep 2) and whether hyperscaler commentary confirms the FY28 ~70% growth claim.

events.title: Salesforce Q2 FY27 AI beat, FY guide raised
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $11.35B, non-GAAP EPS $5.90 (boosted by ~$2.6B Anthropic-related gain), FY2027 revenue raised to $46.1–$46.4B.
events.what_to_watch: Whether software multiples hold after the investment-gain distortion; Agentforce/cRPO quality vs one-off gains.

events.title: Operation Economic Outcast Iran sanctions
events.why_it_matters: Treasury launched sectoral sanctions on Iran digital assets, tech, gold, aviation and shipping plus secondary-sanctions/dollar-exclusion threats after the military campaign.
events.what_to_watch: Enforcement against third-country facilitators (China, Gulf, crypto rails) and any spillover into Hormuz diplomacy.

events.title: US 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian goods in force
events.why_it_matters: After an Aug 18 pause, additional 50% duties on Canadian alcohol, dairy, autos and a wide annex list took effect ~Aug 22, stacking on USMCA goods (~$20–28B of trade).
events.what_to_watch: Canadian dollar-for-dollar retaliation due Sep 8 and any last-minute carve-outs or auto/parts leakage into Detroit supply chains.

events.title: Canada retaliatory tariffs on US goods
events.why_it_matters: Ottawa announced matching retaliation (steel/aluminum, dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp/paper, electronics) effective Sep 8 unless talks reopen.
events.what_to_watch: Final product list, USMCA dispute path, and whether auto/energy exemptions hold.

events.title: CIT upholds IEEPA rescission of $800 de minimis
events.why_it_matters: Court of International Trade (Slip Op. 26-94) held the president could kill the $800 de minimis exemption without imposing 'new' tariffs, keeping duties on low-value e-commerce until the 2027 statutory repeal.
events.what_to_watch: Federal Circuit appeal and CBP enforcement intensity on China/Mexico small parcels.

events.title: National emergency on US bulk-power system
events.why_it_matters: EO declaring a grid-security national emergency can restrict foreign electrical equipment and reshape utility capex/supply chains.
events.what_to_watch: Commerce/DOE implementing rules on transformers, inverters, and China-origin grid kit.

events.title: Beef TRQ expanded 300k tons
events.why_it_matters: Proclamation temporarily raised in-quota lean beef trimmings to ease US retail beef prices after supply shocks.
events.what_to_watch: Packer margins vs cattle prices; limited broad-market impact unless food CPI cools.

events.title: House vote on Senate CR through Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: Senate already passed (90-6, Aug 8) a CR through Dec 11; House GOP aims for a fast-track vote the first week back to avoid a Sep 30 shutdown.
events.what_to_watch: Whether suspension-of-the-rules (2/3) holds, or hardliners force a narrower bill before midterms.

events.title: August NFP / Employment Situation
events.why_it_matters: Consensus ~+55k payrolls (Wolfe ~+65k) after July's -23k print; unemployment seen edging to ~4.2%. Soft labor vs sticky PCE is the Fed's core tension.
events.what_to_watch: Private vs government split, AHE (~+0.2–0.35% MoM), and any benchmark-revision noise.

events.title: August CPI
events.why_it_matters: Last major inflation print before the Sep 15–16 FOMC; July CPI was 3.4% YoY / core 2.5%, while PCE stayed 3.7% — energy and tariffs can reopen the gap.
events.what_to_watch: Core services vs energy; a hot print would cement hike pricing, a cool print would fade Warsh-hawk narratives.

events.title: August PPI
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline inflation print the day before CPI; energy and goods tariffs make PPI a swing input for core goods.
events.what_to_watch: Final-demand ex-food/energy and trade-services components.

events.title: ISM manufacturing PMI and JOLTS
events.why_it_matters: First-week activity and job-openings prints set the tone into NFP; tariffs and energy costs can keep ISM prices-paid elevated even if output is soft.
events.what_to_watch: ISM prices paid/new orders and JOLTS openings vs quits (July data for JOLTS).

events.title: ADP August employment
events.why_it_matters: Private-payroll preview two days before NFP after a weak official July print.
events.what_to_watch: Goods vs services split; large miss would move Sep 4 pricing.

events.title: Hormuz corridor talks vs prolonged oil disruption
events.why_it_matters: Iran war (from ~Feb 28) still throttles Hormuz; Iran–Oman talks on a temporary corridor have pushed Brent to ~$86–87, but flows remain a fraction of pre-war ~18–20 mbpd.
events.what_to_watch: Mine-clearance/corridor implementation vs renewed attacks; any US pause in strikes vs secondary sanctions bite.

events.title: OPEC+ Sept 6 output review (pause after +188k bpd)
events.why_it_matters: Aug 2 deal raises September quotas +188k bpd (completing 2023 voluntary-cut unwind); sources expect a Q4 pause, but Hormuz bottlenecks mean quotas ≠ barrels.
events.what_to_watch: October decision, compliance, and whether the group admits it cannot swing physical supply while Hormuz is impaired.

events.title: Black Sea grain/energy strike spiral
events.why_it_matters: Russia rejected a grain-ship truce; attacks on Odesa-region and Novorossiysk terminals have sent wheat to 3-year highs and hit Russian refining.
events.what_to_watch: Chicago wheat, Ukraine export volumes, and whether food CPI re-accelerates in EM importers.

events.title: ECB decision and new projections (hike priced)
events.why_it_matters: Sources point to a 25 bp hike to 2.50% deposit rate after June's hike to 2.25%; energy-driven HICP ~2.8–3.0% with 2026 GDP projections ~0.8%.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 1 flash HICP, then whether Lagarde signals 'one and done' vs more hikes; Berlin meeting optics.

events.title: Euro area flash HICP (August)
events.why_it_matters: Last inflation snapshot before the Sep 10 ECB meeting; energy from Hormuz is the swing factor vs anchored longer-term expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs core; a 3%+ print would lock in the hike.

events.title: China official manufacturing PMI (August)
events.why_it_matters: July IP slowed to +4.5% YoY and retail to +0.6%; PMI is the first read on whether H2 targeted easing is working after Q2 GDP 4.3%.
events.what_to_watch: 50-line, new orders, and construction-related weakness vs export/NEV strength.

events.title: China July activity miss; LPR held; targeted fiscal
events.why_it_matters: IP +4.5%, retail +0.6% missed; Aug 20 LPR held 3.0%/3.5% (15th month); CNY 800bn policy-financing tool opened applications Aug 24 while PBOC drained MLF but added short-term repos.
events.what_to_watch: Whether applications convert to projects in September or growth keeps sliding toward ~4%.

events.title: BoK hikes 25 bp to 3.00% (back-to-back)
events.why_it_matters: BoK raised to 3.00% and lifted 2026 GDP to 3.3% on semiconductors/AI exports; median 6-month path ~3.25%.
events.what_to_watch: KRW, KOSPI financials, and whether chip-cycle strength offsets tighter domestic rates.

events.title: Broadcom Q3 FY26 earnings (AI ASIC bellwether)
events.why_it_matters: Company guided ~$29.4B revenue / $16B AI semis; Street is aligned (~$29.2–29.5B, EPS ~$3.16–3.30). Post-Nvidia, this is the next AI-capex confirmation.
events.what_to_watch: FY27 AI >$100B reiteration, gross-margin mix, and custom-silicon customer commentary (GOOGL/META/OpenAI).

events.title: Dell, Palo Alto, Medtronic earnings
events.why_it_matters: Dell is an AI-server hardware check; PANW is cyber large-cap; MDT is a healthcare bellwether into a quiet mega-cap week.
events.what_to_watch: Dell server/AI mix and PANW billings; not Mag7 but can move semis/cyber baskets.

events.title: Adobe earnings; Oracle mid-September window
events.why_it_matters: Adobe is confirmed Sep 10 AMC; Oracle IR says Q1 FY27 'mid-September' (calendars cluster Sep 8–14) — software/AI monetization tests after CRM.
events.what_to_watch: Adobe Firefly/AI ARR and Oracle cloud RPO vs capex.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) staggered lockup tranches
events.why_it_matters: June 12 IPO used rolling unlocks; ~90-day tranche around Sep 9–10 adds float after the Aug 20/21 release — largest IPO ever, so supply can hit high-beta risk appetite.
events.what_to_watch: Actual selling vs unlock size; Musk remains locked into 2027.

events.title: SEMICON Taiwan 2026
events.why_it_matters: Largest Asia semi gathering (Taipei Sep 2–4, forums from Aug 31) is where TSMC/toolmakers signal AI packaging, power, and capex into 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Advanced-packaging capacity comments and any China-tool restriction chatter on the sidelines.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure and chip-smuggling enforcement
events.why_it_matters: Han Kuang anti-blockade drills (Aug 5–14), Lai's Aug 23 Kinmen 'peace through strength' speech, plus raids on Nvidia-server smuggling/talent poaching — TSMC risk is slow-burn, not invasion-now.
events.what_to_watch: PLA maritime tempo and any new US export-control cases involving Super Micro/ex-TSMC staff.

events.title: FDA approval of daraxonrasib (Rasonque) for pancreatic cancer
events.why_it_matters: Novel RAS inhibitor approval for metastatic pancreatic cancer is a sector-specific catalyst (Revolution Medicines), not market-wide.
events.what_to_watch: Label, launch uptake, and whether RAS-targeted oncology basket rerates.

events.title: Atlantic TS Dolly; otherwise quiet hurricane season
events.why_it_matters: No 2026 Atlantic hurricane yet (El Niño/shear); Dolly is a weak TS expected to stay a Caribbean rain threat, not a US landfalling hurricane.
events.what_to_watch: NHC upgrades; September climatological peak still exists despite below-normal NOAA outlook.

events.title: UPS Teamsters strike authorization (no walkout yet)
events.why_it_matters: National UPS/UPS Freight units authorized a strike (~93%/91%) during contract talks; leverage event, not an active stoppage.
events.what_to_watch: Ratification fights and any local strike notices into peak season.

events.title: FOMC Sep 15–16 (just beyond window; path set this fortnight)
events.why_it_matters: Hold is base case (~60–70%); hike ~30–40% after sticky PCE and 3 July dissenters. SEP/dots will be the first Warsh-era projections.
events.what_to_watch: NFP (4th) and CPI (11th) inside this scan window will lock the decision; Warsh speech today is the qualitative setup.

events.title: Section 232 tariffs on UAS/drones and parts (100%/25%)
events.why_it_matters: Aug 13 proclamation (FR Aug 19) slaps 100% duties on heavier/thermal UAS and 25% on smaller drones from Sep 3, with allied caps at 15%/10% and an onshoring duty-free program — a China-heavy supply-chain shock the primary never tagged.
events.what_to_watch: CBP/HTS guidance, allied-origin certification, Blue UAS delay to Feb 9 2027, and whether Commerce adds components on a rolling basis.

events.title: BIS DPA order: 100% US allocation of battery black mass and tungsten scrap
events.why_it_matters: Effective Aug 27 through Aug 27 2027, US persons must sell 100% of monthly black-mass e-waste and tungsten scrap to US buyers — first Commerce DPA allocation order, tightening EV-battery and defense-metal feedstock.
events.what_to_watch: BIS exception/hardship grants (14-day clock), CBP export detentions, and Nov 4 comments on expanding the list to other recoverable critical minerals.

events.title: SEC proposes Regulation Crypto Assets (S7-2026-27)
events.why_it_matters: First tailored federal offering regime for non-security crypto subject to investment contracts: $5M startup / $20–75M fundraising exemptions, delinking safe harbor, and blue-sky preemption — a structural US-listing path, not just enforcement.
events.what_to_watch: Federal Register comment deadline (~Oct 20) and whether Congress still moves a market-structure bill alongside the proposal.

events.title: NSPM-17 National Space Transportation Policy
events.why_it_matters: First rewrite since 2013 targets 1,000 US launches/reentries a year by 2030, faster range permitting, US-built vehicles for most government payloads, and commercial lunar/Mars logistics — incremental for launch primes beyond the SpaceX lockup the primary already has.
events.what_to_watch: 90–240 day agency plans on new sites, environmental-review streamlining, and export-control review for launch tech.

events.title: Navy/shipbuilding industrial-base presidential memorandum
events.why_it_matters: Directs a fifth public Navy yard plan (120 days), foreign-yard 'Finland model' investments in US yards, CVN-81 EMALS rollback study, and NAVSEA reform — a multi-year demand signal for GD, HII, and suppliers the primary skipped.
events.what_to_watch: 60-day CVN-81 systems plan and 120-day fifth-yard siting; follow-on Navy Office of the Defense Industrial Base stood up ~Aug 24.

events.title: NDRC draft outbound-investment administrative measures
events.why_it_matters: First major rewrite of 2017/18 outbound-FDI rules adds adverse-event reporting (foreign tech/data discrimination), large reinvestment disclosure, and security screening — a capital-outflow and overseas M&A friction for Chinese corporates.
events.what_to_watch: Public comment through Sep 20 and whether final text tightens approvals vs. just reporting.

events.title: UMich August final sentiment / inflation expectations
events.why_it_matters: Prelim crashed to 51.0 from 55.2 with 1-year inflation expectations at 4.3% and 5–10y stuck at 3.3% — the inflation-expectations print Warsh's Jackson Hole audience will have in hand, and the primary omitted it.
events.what_to_watch: Final 10:00 ET confirmation vs. prelim and any revision to long-run expectations.

events.title: Japan Q2 GDP first preliminary: +0.3% q/q / +1.1% annualized miss
events.why_it_matters: Third straight expansion but well below ~2% annualized consensus as private consumption slipped and net exports did the heavy lifting — a BoJ/JPY input the primary never listed.
events.what_to_watch: Second preliminary on Sep 8 and whether consumption stays negative.

events.title: UK July CPI +2.9% YoY (released Aug 19)
events.why_it_matters: CPI accelerated from 2.6% on energy pass-through, keeping BoE hike risk alive even as markets still price a Sep 17 hold at 3.75%.
events.what_to_watch: August CPI on Sep 16 (just beyond window) and whether second-round wage effects show up.

events.title: July housing starts -12.4% to 1.239M (released Aug 18)
events.why_it_matters: Sharp MoM drop in starts is a rates/tariff-sensitive activity miss the primary's US data stack (PCE, NFP, CPI, ISM, JOLTS, ADP) did not include.
events.what_to_watch: August starts/permits into NFP week and whether permits confirm a downshift.

events.title: July industrial production +0.2%; capacity utilization 76.3%
events.why_it_matters: Soft +0.2% MoM (below ~0.3% consensus) with utilization still subdued is a second-tier activity check on tariff/energy cost pass-through into goods.
events.what_to_watch: August IP into mid-September and ISM prices-paid vs. output split on Sep 1.

events.title: Eurozone August flash PMI composite 52.1 (9-month high)
events.why_it_matters: Manufacturing 52.8 and new orders at a 40-month high cut against the energy-shock narrative heading into Sep 1 HICP and the Sep 10 ECB hike the primary already has.
events.what_to_watch: Final PMI vs. flash and whether export orders survive Hormuz freight costs.

events.title: US 10-year / 30-year Treasury reopenings
events.why_it_matters: Tentative Q3 schedule: $39B 10s on Sep 9 and $22B 30s on Sep 10, settling Sep 15 — duration supply into CPI (Sep 11) and the Sep 16 FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Tail ratios vs. the Aug 12–13 refunding (10s ~4.683% high yield) and any buyback offset.

events.title: CrowdStrike Q2 FY27: record $333M net-new ARR, FY guide raised
events.why_it_matters: Cyber bellwether printed $1.47B revenue (+26%), $5.84B ARR, record FCF, and a 630 bp lift to FY net-new ARR growth — the software/security read-through the primary skipped beside NVDA/CRM.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through into PANW (Sep 1) and Zscaler (Sep 3) prints.

events.title: Deere Q3 FY26 beat; FY net-income guide raised to $4.75–$5.00B
events.why_it_matters: Ag-equipment cycle bellwether: EPS $5.10 on $12.6B sales, construction/turf offsetting weak large-ag, management calling FY26 the cycle bottom — missed second-tier earnings.
events.what_to_watch: Early-order books and Brazil/Europe demand vs. US construction strength.

summary: CARRIED FORWARD from 2026-08-28: both scan passes failed for 2026-08-30; these are the previous still-live events.
